rule: **Who gets a Mark** (lead's rule 10-17 + recorded calls): a distinct model = a checkpoint deployed live, used as the init / graft source of another run, or evaluated as a candidate (it got its own verdict vs a baseline). One Mark per training configuration; its seed replicates, intermediate snapshots, controls that never got a promotion verdict, smokes, failed launches, test scaffolding (rltest) and opponent / exploiter policies stay unmarked but are recorded with their relation. A same-run checkpoint gets its own Mark only when it was deployed, used as an init, or was an explicit continuation with its own verdict (LONGER). A raw checkpoint and its grafted twin are one Mark (two files). **Numbering**: per deck, chronological by the checkpoint's creation (earliest mtime of any byte-identical copy; HANDOFF date for the two no-file Marks). **Word**: the change vs the parent Mark (its init); siblings from one parent are named by the change their arm tested; scratch-trained models (no init) are named by the change vs the model they were compared with (shown as 'compared to').
